script_sections.title: Opening
script_sections.content:
Good morning, neighbours and friends.

Welcome to our Independence Day gathering. Today we remember 15 August 1947 — not as a date in a textbook, but as a promise we still keep: that this colony of homes, this society, this country, belongs to all of us.

Before we begin, a request: phones on silent, hearts on full volume. We have a flag to hoist, songs to sing, and a few games so the kids don't outrun the uncles.

I am [HOST NAME], and it is my honour to walk us through the morning.

script_sections.title: Flag Hoisting
script_sections.content:
We now invite [CHIEF GUEST / SOCIETY PRESIDENT] to hoist the national flag.

Please stand. Those who can, please face the flag.

[Pause for hoisting]

We will now sing the National Anthem. Please remain standing until it ends.

[Jana Gana Mana]

Thank you. You may be seated.

A reminder from the flag code: the Tiranga is not a costume, not a selfie prop, and not something we let touch the ground. Treat it the way we treat the people who earned it.

script_sections.title: Segment Transitions
script_sections.content:
INTO SONGS: The anthem is our official voice. What comes next is our unofficial one — the songs we grew up humming on the radio, in school assemblies, and in traffic. First up is our planned patriotic set. If you submitted a song, you're in the running order I'll announce in a moment.

INTO ICEBREAKERS: Standing still is patriotic. Moving around is also patriotic, especially if it stops the aunties from forming a complaint committee. Let's play a few short games — nothing that requires a degree, everything that requires a smile.

INTO CLOSING: We've hoisted, we've sung, we've slightly embarrassed ourselves in public. That is a successful 15th August. Stay for tea; leave with the feeling that this society is more than a WhatsApp group.

script_sections.title: Closing / Vote of Thanks
script_sections.content:
A short vote of thanks.

To [CHIEF GUEST] for hoisting the flag.
To every volunteer who set up chairs, speakers, and the tea table before the rest of us found our slippers.
To the children who practised songs louder than the adults practised patience.
To every resident who showed up — presence is the real decoration.

Jai Hind. Please join us for refreshments. The national anthem is over; the national snack is not.

songs.title: Jana Gana Mana
songs.note: National Anthem — play immediately after flag hoisting. Full version, everyone standing.

songs.title: Vande Mataram
songs.note: Great for the flag-hoisting moment or right after the anthem, before speeches.

songs.title: Ae Watan — Raazi
songs.note: Modern patriotic number; works well if you have a soloist or a kids' choir.

songs.title: Sandese Aate Hain
songs.note: Border — emotional middle of the programme; keep tissues near the aunties.

songs.title: Maa Tujhe Salaam
songs.note: A.R. Rahman — strong closer before vote of thanks if the crowd is still standing.

activities.title: Name That Freedom Fighter
activities.description: Host reads a one-line clue ("lawyer from Porbandar", "nightingale of India"). First team to shout the name scores a point. Keep it to 8 clues so it stays brisk. Prize: extra samosa.

activities.title: Tiranga Outfit Relay
activities.description: Three teams. Each team must assemble saffron, white, and green using only items already on people (dupattas, caps, bags). First complete 'flag' wins. No buying, no leaving the lawn.

activities.title: Two Truths and a Tricolour Lie
activities.description: Volunteers share two true facts about their family and Independence Day plus one lie. Audience votes. Classic icebreaker, patriotic twist.

activities.title: Human Map of India
activities.description: Kids stand where they think their home state sits on an imaginary map of India. Host 'corrects' the geography. Loud, funny, photo-friendly.

activities.title: Jai Hind Speed Intro
activities.description: Each person has 15 seconds: name, wing/flat, and one thing they love about India that is not food. Timer is strict. Great for mixing wings that never talk.
